cl Abstract We present D-v2v, a new dynamic (one-pass) variable-to-variable compressor
In D-v2v, we process the input text word-wise to gather variable-length symbols that can be either terminals (new words) or non-terminals, subsequences of words seen before in the input text
Our D- v2v permits real-time transmission of data, i
Our experiments show that D-v2v is able to overcome the compression ratios of the v2vDC, the state-of-the-art semi-static variable-to-variable compressor, and to almost reach p7zip values
1 Introduction Text compression has gained relevance in the last decades along with the growth of text databases
The first compressors based on Huffman coding [1] using character-oriented mod- eling obtained rather poor compression ratios ontext collections (compression around 60%)

However, when Huffman coding was coupled with a word-based modeler dur- ing the 80s [2] the compression ratio obtained by those semi-static compressors was close to 25% when applied to English texts, and they set the basis to build modern text retrieval systems over them [3]
